mcu_0160_08009954.name: mcu_edge_counter_step
mcu_0160_08009954.summary: Advance a bidirectional phase counter one step and return its selected edge output bit
mcu_0160_08009954.description: Steps a counter structure and returns one output bit. Layout: u32 count at +0x00, u32 limit at +0x04, u32 reload at +0x08, u8 mode at +0x0c, u8 phase at +0x0d (0 = low, 1 = high, 2 = not yet defined), u8 last-edge latch at +0x0e, u8 output at +0x0f, u8 enable at +0x10. If the enable byte is 0 it returns 0 and changes nothing. Up-step (direction != 0): count is incremented until it reaches limit; at the limit the phase is set to 1 and count is reloaded from the reload value. Down-step: count is decremented, and when it is already 0 the phase is cleared to 0. The latch is set to 0 on a 0 to 1 phase transition and to 1 on a 1 to 0 transition. Output mode: 1 = phase high, 2 = rising edge, 3 = falling edge, 4 = any edge, 5 = phase high with latch 0, 6 = phase low with latch 1, other = 0. Modes 2 to 4 compare the phase before and after this step; modes 5 and 6 use the updated latch. It is one of a small group with mcu_edge_counter_init, mcu_edge_counter_reset and mcu_edge_counter_force_high, which operate on the same structure. Called from about a dozen motor-control sites (for example mcu_0160_08003434, mcu_0160_08008a14).

params.name: param_2
params.description: direction: nonzero counts up, zero counts down

mcu_0160_08009954.notes: The algorithm is clear from the code. The meaning of phase, mode and output in the motor control is a guess.

mcu_0160_0800a2ac.name: SystemInit

Steps: enable the PWC clock (CRM APB1EN bit 28, PWCEN), set bit 2 of the byte at 0x40007050 (an address outside the PWC block in the repo SVD, not named), then disable the PWC clock. Then CRM->CTRL |= HICKEN and wait for HICKSTBL; select HICK as system clock (CFG.SCLKSEL = 0) and wait for SCLKSTS = 0; clear HEXTEN, HEXTBYPS, CFDEN and PLLEN (CTRL &= ~0x010D0000); set CFG = 0; PLL = 0x1F10; MISC1 = 0x00100000; and CLKINT = 0x009F0000 to clear the stability and CFD flags. If the descriptor's pending bit (bit 0 of desc word 0) is set, it first checks bit (4 * channel - 3) of status word 0. If that bit is clear it clears the busy flag and returns. If it is set, it sets the same bit in status word 1 as a latch and clears the descriptor's pending bit. Then, if the ring's read index (+0x404) differs from its write index (+0x405), it resets the 32-bit idle counter at +0x604, points desc word 3 at slot+8 and desc word 1 at the slot length (slot+4; each slot is 0x100 bytes), sets the pending bit, advances the read index modulo 4 and increments the count at +0x406. Otherwise, if the descriptor is not pending, it increments the 32-bit idle counter at +0x604 and saturates it at 20 (0x14). It then clears the busy flag and returns.

mcu_0160_0800b71a.description: Replaces CTRL2 bit 0 (ADCEN) with bit 0 of the argument, by read-modify-write. It does not wait for the ADC stabilisation time after enabling; any such wait is the caller's job. Called from mcu_0160_08001fb0.

mcu_0160_0800b724.name: mcu_store_inverted_word
mcu_0160_0800b724.summary: Store the bitwise complement of the argument into a word
mcu_0160_0800b724.description: Writes ~value to *p. This is the same operation as mcu_store_inverted_mask_0x10, but with the destination passed directly rather than at a fixed offset. It keeps a mask in complemented form. Called from mcu_0160_08001ee4 and mcu_0160_0800226c.

params.name: param_2
params.description: value to store, complemented before the write
